lead.headline: Ukraine sinks Russian warship in Libyan port, widening the war
lead.hook: Ukraine says seven naval drones sank Russia's corvette Merkury in Libya's Benghazi port on Sunday, about 1,500 miles from the frontline, and also hit the cargo ship MV Angara.
points: Zelenskyy said a Russian Ka-27 helicopter was also destroyed. Satellite imagery shows the corvette mostly capsized. The SBU says the drones launched from a mothership.
The Merkury, commissioned in 2023, had docked under a Russia-eastern Libya agreement to refuel while escorting cargo ships that could carry military supplies, the ISW says.

The day before, the cargo ship Sparta II was hit in the Gulf of Finland; Finland's military assessed Ukraine likely struck it. Kyiv has not claimed it. At least four Russian vessels were reportedly hit in November.

Libya's eastern administration called it a sovereignty violation and sought a UN investigation. The UN mission in Libya wants an independent probe. The Kremlin called it a 'very dangerous trend' and warned of 'painful' consequences.
Analysts say the Mediterranean is now an external theatre and warn of added risk to global shipping already strained near Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb.

frontpage.headline: US blacklists Megaspeed, the firm at the centre of the Nvidia scandal
frontpage.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
frontpage.hook: Commerce added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six entities in Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia to its Entity List, barring them from buying advanced AI chips without a US licence.
points: Commerce cites a significant risk that they divert advanced computing items to unauthorised users. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.
The US inquiry began in 2024. Nvidia put Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025, but Commerce never blacklisted it, drawing pressure from lawmakers and Treasury Secretary Bessent.
A former NSC official said the rule omits a footnote extending bans to foreign-made items containing US technology. BIS says all AI chips are covered anyway.
Last week Commerce required licences for data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil exporting advanced chips.
Export bills including the AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act and MATCH Act may be attached to year-end defence legislation.
frontpage.evidence_of: US tightens chip export rules after the Nvidia scandal

frontpage.headline: COP31 ends without a main pact after fossil-fuel row
frontpage.hook: COP31 in Antalya became the longest ever, running nearly 50 hours over, and failed to adopt its 'Antalya pact' after at least 32 countries rejected it.
points: The EU, UK and small island states objected that the draft omitted fossil fuels and gave no clear adaptation-finance figure, including a proposed $120bn target.
Petrostates such as Saudi Arabia pushed to drop fossil-fuel references and insert carbon capture at gigatonne scale by 2035. The EU said talks were hijacked.
Other items passed: just transition work programme, global goal on adaptation, climate finance work programme and carbon markets.
Around 80 nations backed 35% of final energy from electricity by 2035. Next year's COP is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

frontpage.headline: Trump says he 'convinced' Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang
frontpage.hook: Nvidia shares jumped about 31% on Monday after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after he resigned over affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy.
points: Trump told CNBC 'I convinced them'; VP Vance helped lobby. The board cited input from senior US officials that Huang poses no national security risk.
The S&P 500 rose 4.7% and Nasdaq Composite about 6.5%. Nvidia added roughly $1 trillion in value yet is still about 23% below its 28 October close.
Huang testifies to House committees on 1 December and the Senate Banking Committee on 3 December. Democrats and some Republicans criticised the move.
Nvidia says an independent investigation into the alleged Chinese intelligence operation continues.
frontpage.evidence_of: The AI trade drives markets, and now the dollar and rate bets

frontpage.headline: India-EU trade deal likely signed in December, in force by mid-2027
frontpage.hook: The EU ambassador says the India-EU free trade agreement is likely to be signed in December and take effect around mid-2027, covering EUR 118 billion of goods trade in 2025.
points: Talks concluded in January; teams are doing technical refining. EU ministers must approve signing, then the European Parliament votes yes or no without reopening talks.
The Parliament's foreign affairs chair expects a view in spring.
Tariffs on about $33 billion of Indian labour-intensive exports, such as textiles, leather and gems, drop to zero.
India protected dairy, cereals and poultry. The pact also covers services and professional mobility.

frontpage.headline: Fine air pollution raises dementia risk 25%, study finds
frontpage.hook: People in the most polluted third of regions were 25% more likely to develop dementia than those in the cleanest third, in about 475,000 UK Biobank adults tracked up to 14 years.
points: The link held regardless of inherited genetic risk, after adjusting for age, smoking and diabetes.
Mice breathing concentrated PM2.5 (fine particles) for five months had leaky blood-brain barriers, inflammation and lost newborn neurons in the hippocampus.
Memory problems appeared even in healthy mice without amyloid plaques; in Alzheimer's-prone mice, plaques built up faster.

frontpage.headline: Parliament's monsoon session unprorogued for a record 102 days
frontpage.hook: Parliament's monsoon session has stayed unprorogued 102 days since 13 August, a record, with no winter session dates announced.
points: The opposition says the government is delaying the winter session so it can reconvene quickly under Rule 15 to pass a delimitation bill.
The NDA denies this, says scheduling is the government's prerogative and reaffirms commitment to the women's quota bill.

frontpage.headline: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal after August floods
frontpage.hook: India announced a $1.62bn package for Nepal, one of its largest relief commitments, as PM Balendra Shah made his first bilateral visit since taking office in March.
points: It includes a $377m grant for reconstruction and infrastructure and a $1.24bn line of credit for energy projects.
August's glacier-collapse floods killed over 1,300 people, with more than 5,000 missing. The UN loss and damage fund set aside $20m.
India supplies over 60% of Nepal's imports ($8.6bn) against China's 13%, and competes with China for influence.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix and approve code
stories.hook: Claude Ship lets AI agents approve routine code changes under policies a team writes, with two of its three parts in beta.
points: Code Review is generally available. PR Steward (beta) fixes failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review feedback, and comments on what it changed and how to roll back.
Claude Approvals (beta) applies a natural-language policy stored in the repository, weighing Code Review findings and Anthropic's classifiers.
Anthropic suggests observe-only mode first, one repository and monthly spending limits. Teams choose review depth and which changes go to humans.
It runs on GitHub for Claude Team and Enterprise plans, aimed at the review bottleneck as AI writes more code.

stories.headline: Amazon buys Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B
stories.hook: Amazon is paying $7.5 billion for Israeli startup Decart, per Bloomberg, taking its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), which runs models efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon and Google hardware.
points: Amazon also gets Decart's founding team and researchers. Decart builds real-time world models, most recently Oasis 3, and AI video tools.
Amazon is preparing to sell its Trainium chips to customers as a Nvidia rival; Decart's tech could ease moving workloads onto them.

stories.headline: Chinese military fears AI could let US find its nuclear missiles
stories.hook: Chinese military researchers say AI could cut US decision time from 15-30 minutes to 90 seconds, threatening China's guaranteed second-strike deterrent, per a New York Times analysis.
points: China has about 620 operational warheads, per the Federation of American Scientists, and is expected to reach roughly 1,000 by 2030.
Chinese institutes are studying AI-controlled flight paths for hypersonic missiles.
Earlier this year the US military nearly boarded a Chinese ship on a false AI-generated intelligence report.
AI in nuclear systems was not discussed at the Xi-Trump-Putin summit; the US and China have made almost no progress on safeguards.

stories.headline: India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6B in Jan-Sept 2026
stories.hook: India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in nine months of 2026, up 96% from $822 million a year earlier, per Tracxn, the highest nine-month total since 2019.
points: Deals fell to 87 from 149, so large rounds drove it: the top ten raised $1.5 billion, 90% of the total.
Neysa raised $600 million (37% of funding); Sarvam raised $255 million and $90.4 million; Yotta $150 million.
Series A and later rounds fell 33% to 24; first-time funded companies fell 60% to 24; investors fell to 111 from 169.
Globally AI companies raised $383.5 billion, so India's share is 0.4%, ninth among countries.

also.line: Anthropic is now xAI's biggest compute rental customer, per the NYT. xAI has rented compute to rivals since May, and its June IPO raised pressure for revenue.

stories.headline: Megaspeed blacklist lands as Huang returns to Nvidia
stories.hook: The US put Megaspeed International and six Southeast Asian entities on its trade blacklist hours after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, with goods in transit getting a 30-day grace period.
points: The listed entities include Swiftdata, Apex Enterprise Solutions, Speedmatrix, MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International and Megaspeed (Thailand). Commerce and Justice are jointly investigating possible criminal export violations.
Malaysia says PT Megaspeed is not a Malaysian entity and will warn data centre operators. Singapore's PM said the city-state did not want to be 'used and abused'.
Critics note Washington blacklists a middleman while licensing Nvidia H200 sales to China directly with a 25% government cut. Bessent says other departments wanted the listing for months.
stories.evidence_of: US tightens chip export rules after the Nvidia scandal

stories.headline: IBM quantum computer does in 15 minutes what classical methods cannot
stories.hook: IBM and the University of Chicago ran a calculation on 70 logical qubits in about 15 minutes that leading classical simulation methods would need impractically long to reproduce.
points: The team says it also established statistical confidence in the result's accuracy, tackling the verification problem of quantum advantage.
The run used 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 T gates. Error correction cut logical error rates tenfold below physical ones.
It was designed to show advantage, not solve a real-world problem.

stories.headline: China humanoid robot stocks draw over 10 billion yuan in a day
stories.hook: China's A-share humanoid robot sector rose nearly 6% on 23 November with over 10.2 billion yuan (about $1.5 billion) of net inflows, after policy support and cheaper margin financing.
points: Four ministries encouraged elderly-care robots, and five humanoid standards took effect. Exchanges cut minimum margin ratios from 100% to 80%.

Unitree hit its 20% daily limit, valued at 286.4 billion yuan, up about 75% from its 15 October low. Its Q3 revenue rose 69.9%, but profit excluding one-offs fell 18.8% for the nine months as R&D spending jumped.
Goldman Sachs forecasts 75,000 humanoid shipments globally in 2026. China's output is expected to top 100,000 units this year.
Goldman's Shanghai seat sold a net 213 million yuan on Unitree the same day.

stories.headline: China's Z.ai uses looped transformers for its new model
stories.hook: Z.ai says its 750-billion-parameter GLM-5.4 matches models two to four times its size by using a looped transformer, which reruns the same layers several times.
points: It is the first major Chinese model to disclose the technique, after reports that OpenAI adopted it. Z.ai withheld detailed benchmark scores.
The loop deepens reasoning without more parameters or compute, and visible reasoning output fell up to 14%.
Safety researchers warn that reasoning hidden inside loops is harder to monitor. Z.ai restricted access and will open-source later after safety hardening.
A 3-trillion-parameter model is planned by year-end, per a JPMorgan note.

stories.headline: India set to miss most 2030 EV targets, says BNEF
stories.hook: BloombergNEF says India will miss 2030 electrification targets in every vehicle segment except three-wheelers, even as passenger EV sales rise 42% in 2026 to over 305,000.
points: EVs are 6.7% of passenger vehicle sales and BNEF expects 10.2% (621,000 units) by 2030. Electric two-wheelers were 9.4% of sales this year, boosted by fuel prices after the Iran war.
Only 1.5% of medium and heavy commercial vehicle sales are projected electric by 2030.
Road fuel demand is __projected to peak above 2.5 million barrels a day__ in 2034.
India may need over 8.7 million charging connectors by 2040, about $29 billion.

stories.headline: India hits record solar share in October, but coal still leans on weak monsoon
stories.hook: Solar supplied a record 12% of India's electricity in October, per CREA, yet a weaker El Niño monsoon cut hydropower and raised coal use.
points: India's solar generation matched Australia's or Italy's total output that month.
Storage and wind are needed to improve reliability.
China's thermal generation fell 7.3%, a fourth monthly fall, while it added 58.7 GW of thermal capacity in eight months.
In OECD countries, clean generation growth met all demand growth in nine months, while fossil generation fell only slightly.

also.line: Amazon pledges $7 billion for renewable energy projects in India by 2030, on top of $4 billion already contracted, expanding its Indian clean power supply.

stories.headline: Weak monsoon and low fertiliser use likely to cut wheat output
stories.hook: Wheat sowing is down 15% in a year, and fertiliser use is falling, which points to lower output from the world's second-largest producer.
points: Weak southwest and northeast monsoons reduced soil moisture; farmers are shifting to other crops. Haryana saw the biggest drop, then Uttar Pradesh; Madhya Pradesh rose.
April-October use fell: urea about 4%, NPK over 25%, super phosphate over 5%, potash 11%. DAP rose 1.6% as farmers substituted for scarce cheaper urea.
The Fertilizers Association says output will fall but less than some predict. Lower production could affect domestic food inflation.

stories.headline: WFP warns war chokepoints could raise its costs $727 million
stories.hook: WFP head Luke Lindberg warned shipping chokepoints tied to Middle East and Ukraine wars could raise the agency's costs by $727 million by mid-2027, jeopardising food aid for 7.3 million more people (summary from limited source text).
points: Lindberg said it is untenable to have full grain silos in Ukraine and Poland while stomachs are empty elsewhere.

stories.headline: olee.space wins DRDO contract for laser-link drone communication
stories.hook: Pune startup olee.space must build a laser-link drone communication system for DRDO within 18 months, carrying two-way data between ground stations and drones in flight.
points: It will design ground and airborne free-space optical terminals with automatic pointing, acquisition and tracking, a tripod ground unit plus a compact drone payload.
The company says laser links resist radio jamming and interception, unlike radio. In Ukraine, jamming pushed drones to trail fibre cables, which limit range and can snag.
Co-founder James Solomon says holding a laser link on a moving drone is one of the hardest communications problems; work began a year ago.

stories.headline: Dollar near 20-month high as AI rally fuels Fed hike bets
stories.hook: The dollar hovered near a 20-month high on Tuesday after Jensen Huang's reinstatement revived the AI rally and stoked expectations of Fed hikes (summary from limited source text).
points: Reports say the recovery in AI stocks raised expectations for the Fed.
stories.evidence_of: The AI trade drives markets, and now the dollar and rate bets

also.line: Malaysia's PM Anwar says US curbs on advanced AI chips for China will not stop Malaysia working with Beijing and Chinese firms, per an SCMP interview.
also.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News

stories.headline: India's gold imports fall 40% in April-October
stories.hook: India imported $24.7 billion of gold in April-October, down from $41.24 billion a year earlier, a fall of $16.46 billion, per trader body CTI.
points: Gold imports were about $72 billion in 2025-26; 2026-27 is estimated at $35-40 billion.
CTI's Goyal credits Modi's appeal to cut purchases and lower prices: about Rs 1.25 crore per kg from about Rs 1.90 crore at the time of the appeal.
The wedding season is expected to generate about Rs 6 lakh crore of business over roughly 52 lakh weddings, with jewellery 8-10%.

also.line: At the UN Security Council, India invoked the 1943 Bengal famine to say conflict costs fall on the Global South. WFP says about 10 million tonnes of Russian and Ukrainian wheat may not reach markets.
also.source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu

stories.headline: EU proposes 22nd Russia sanctions package, including sports ban
stories.source: Al Jazeera – Breaking News, World News and Video from Al Jazeera
stories.hook: The European Commission proposed its 22nd Russia sanctions package, which would cut 60 banks from SWIFT and bar Russian teams and athletes competing under its flag at EU events.
points: It sets up a crypto sanctions task force and bans visas for Russians who fought in Ukraine.
It restricts Russian sponsor funding to EU sports and cultural bodies and bars Russians from leading sports federations.
All 27 members must endorse it. The EU has sanctioned over 4,200 people and entities, a month after listing about 1,600 more.

stories.headline: Brain shows a shared meaning component across 21 languages
stories.hook: fMRI data from speakers of 21 languages across 8 families show models trained on some languages predict brain responses in unseen ones, pointing to a shared meaning component.
points: Researchers combined existing data (12 languages) with new scans (9 languages) and used multilingual AI model representations to predict language-network activity.
Generalisation to unseen languages held across language family, stimulus type and presentation modality.

stories.headline: Wernicke's area builds a word 'blueprint' before we speak
stories.hook: UCSF researchers found neurons in part of Wernicke's area activate about 250 milliseconds before speech to plan word features such as length and frequency.
points: The signal passes to frontal planning areas and the motor cortex; hearing and speech-planning neurons sit side by side. Stimulation and lesion analyses confirmed a causal role.
In two paralysed participants, signals from this region decoded both attempted and heard words, offering an alternative target for speech brain-computer interfaces.

stories.headline: Brain serotonin acts as a brake on movement with age
stories.hook: Blocking an age-strengthened serotonin pathway restored youthful activity, speed and grip strength in older mice, suggesting the ageing brain brakes movement rather than running out of fuel.
points: Adults aged 50-70 walked slower and carried more fat than those aged 17-30, a pattern mice mirrored.
Higher serotonin signalling suppresses dopamine, which drives the urge to move.
Treated older mice gained lean muscle and lost body fat. The work is in mice only.

also.line: A remotely operated submarine found the deepest known evidence of explosive volcanic activity in the Mariana trench; researchers say its nature is unusual and worth further exploration.

stories.headline: 72% of India's tech workers would switch careers, Blind survey finds
stories.hook: 72% of 2,958 India-based tech professionals would switch to a completely different career if it cost nothing, and only 13% are happy where they are, per Blind.
points: 42% would switch if pay stayed the same; 30% __would switch immediately. 56% would not encourage__ their children into tech.
Only 4% would recommend software engineering to a young person; healthcare led at 34%, then AI/ML at 19%, government jobs at 15%.
Desire to leave was highest at Intuit (89%) and Goldman Sachs (87%). Blind posts about leaving software engineering are up 37.5% on all of 2025.
The survey does not show AI directly caused the desire to leave.

also.line: foundit projects India's white-collar hiring to grow 8.16% in 2027 to 1.38 crore jobs, up from 3.30% in 2026; entry-level hiring is forecast at 4.64%, up from 0.69%.

stories.headline: South Korea briefly issues air-raid warning after Russian jets approach
stories.hook: South Korea scrambled fighters after Russian warplanes entered its air defence zone, and a mix-up triggered a three-minute air-raid warning for about 9,000 residents of Ulleung Island.
points: The jets did not enter territorial airspace. The interior ministry wrongly said they had, and a provincial message wrongly called them North Korean, corrected about 40 minutes later.
Seoul will summon Russia's military attaché. A similar incursion occurred on 17 November.

also.line: The World Chess Championship between D Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov begins; both players attended the press conference and opening ceremony at the Palais des Nations on 22 November.

opportunities.name: Primewise Founders Club Networking Event
opportunities.summary: In-person meetup with 20+ selected founders and investors. A confirmation form is required before registering; the listing says Jaipur but the text mentions Gurgaon, so check the location.

opportunities.name: Zero-G Hacks
opportunities.summary: Online 3D modelling and additive-manufacturing competition for students; prizes of $60, $40 and $20 Amazon gift cards. No 3D printer required.

patterns.name: US tightens chip export rules after the Nvidia scandal
patterns.line: Commerce put Megaspeed and six affiliates in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand on its Entity List (trade blacklist), a week after licence rules for Southeast Asian data centres. Bipartisan export bills may ride on year-end defence legislation.

evidence.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, targeting firm central to Nvidia crisis
US places Megaspeed on blacklist as Jensen Huang returns to helm of Nvidia

patterns.why: Chip buyers and cloud hosts in Southeast Asia now carry know-your-customer risk. Nvidia faces more Congress scrutiny; China-linked operators lose a route to advanced chips.
patterns.watch: Whether the export bills get attached to the year-end defence bill.

patterns.name: The AI trade drives markets, and now the dollar and rate bets
patterns.line: Nvidia's reinstated CEO lifted Nvidia about 31%, the Nasdaq Composite 6.5% and the S&P 500 4.7% in one day. The dollar sits near a 20-month high as the rebound feeds Fed hike bets.

evidence.title: Trump tells CNBC he was represented at Nvidia board, spoke to Huang
Dollar climbs as renewed AI euphoria fuels Fed hike bets

patterns.why: US growth and stock wealth lean on AI spending, so one firm's governance news moves currencies and rate expectations. A stronger dollar and higher rates squeeze emerging markets such as India.
patterns.watch: Whether the dollar holds its 20-month high as Fed hike bets build.

takeaways.line: With consensus blocked, COP outcomes shift to voluntary coalitions such as the roughly 80 nations backing 35% electrification by 2035. Progress comes from willing countries, not unanimous texts.
takeaways.title: COP31: Key outcomes agreed at the UN climate talks in Antalya

takeaways.line: Amazon paying for software that runs models efficiently on any chip suggests selling Trainium chips depends on making Nvidia-trained workloads easy to move.
takeaways.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
